136126.overview: The goal is to guide miner Willy through a series of caverns in his quest for fortune (and a high score). In each cavern he must collect all the keys to unlock the exit, and then make his escape before the air runs out. The caverns are populated by dangerous robots of quite amazing designs, and the platforms pose additional problems that must be solved.

136425.overview:
Moon Cresta is a vertical scrolling shoot-'em-up. The action involves the player moving their ship along the base of the screen, while wave after wave of aliens come towards it. The yellow aliens split when shot, while the magenta ones are the toughest of all. Once the coast is clear, the player must attempt to manually dock their ship in a limited amount of time. Docking successfully will earn the player bonus points.

The Dragon 32 port of the Arcade game was by John Martin and Incentive Software.

136599.overview: Mined-Out involves guiding a character across a screen covered with mines. He can move in any of the four main directions. At each point, he is told how many of these four squares have mines in, but not the exact locations of the mines, making completion a precarious challenge. There are 8 skill levels, each with progressively more and more mines. After each level, you are showed an 'action replay' of your path, as well as a full diagram of where each mine was.

137918.overview:
You have been sent to break the power of the evil Dungeon Lord. On your shoulders rests the fate of all your people. If you fail, they will fall under the thrall of the Dungeon Lord forever; you are their last and only hope.

Once the game is in progress, you will have to search the passages and chambers of the dungeon until you have overcome all the monsters in the maze before meeting the Dungeon Lord in the final battle to the death.

161899.overview: The invaders are attacking the Earth with their new hyper missiles which never miss. It is up to you to defend the world and the people.

164981.overview:
A bold adventurer descends into the enormous labyrinth of the Cretan King Minos at Knossos, hoping to part seven mythical monsters (including the terrifying, titular, Minotaur) from sixteen treasures and escape with his life, helped only by a handful of arcane spells acquired while navigating dead ends and the enigmatic ramblings of an inspired Oracle wandering the maze.

It's not entirely fair to blame the period hardware limitations for this game's poorly-aged VERB NOUN text parser, as Infocom first launched home versions of Zork I a year earlier, but at the time its grammar was still industry-standard par for the course. What made this title stand out is also what kept its adherents on their toes (... for decades) -- inconstant internal rules and conditions that changed every time the game was played.

Much like the color of potions in Nethack shuffling their associations with spell effects between games, this game not only jumbles the relation between spell names and their effects, but also the conditions that must be met in order to learn them! Similarly unpredictable are the locations and vulnerabilities of monsters and treasures. Add to that a huge (four floors of 64 rooms each) maze full of one-way passages, bogus "dummy" treasures, realtime monster movement, unreliable and abstruse room connections and you end up with a devious dungeon indeed.

175423.overview:
Mudpies is best described as a single screen, overhead, arcade shooter played for high scores.

Similar in style to Robotron the player takes control of Arnold, a young boy who has disrupted a circus by throwing pies at the clowns. The clowns however are not happy and soon they begin throwing things back.

By controlling Arnold, the player must navigate around the play area avoiding angry clowns and hitting them with pies to collect points. Clowns will attack by throwing juggling clubs and if hit by a clown or club will be sent to the First Aid tend and loose a life. Three trips to First Aid and it's game over (extra visits awarded for each 10,000 points scored).

Arnold also has a food meter to keep an eye on which must be replenished to keep him moving. Picking up burgers, fries and shakes are just what he needs but overfeeding is just as bad as under feeding however and if the meter gets too low or high he will slow to half speed.

There are six main rooms in the game which can be left when the doors become open, some rooms are Random Challenge rooms and have no pies to pick up for ammunition. If you can get out without getting caught you are awarded big bonus points. Also, after every 20,000 points you can exit into the Mudslinging Round, here the clowns are stationary and do not attack but are still deadly if ran into.

The game has support for two players with play alternating between each life lost.

175425.overview: Mr Dig is based on the arcade game Mr. Do! where you have to collect all the cherries over various single screen levels to move to the next level. As you move through the tunnels or dig through the dirt there are various nasties chasing you, but they can only move through tunnels and can't dig. To stop them you can either throw a bouncing ball where only one can be thrown at a time, or remove the dirt below an apple and make it fall on top of them. If you are touched by a nasty then you lose one of five lives and when all are gone it's game over. Before you play you can select a skill level from 1 to 9.

175712.overview: You have discovered an old map and a ships log book indicating the existence of magnificent treasures (including a mysterious ruby, the Java Star) aboard an 18th century sailing ship, that sank in the Caribbean. You must organise an expedition, gathering resources and information, before making your perilous journey across the Atlantic...

216289.overview:
In the advert, Monsters is described as "a superb version of the Arcade game Dig Dug-Panic", and indeed it is a clone of Space Panic. On a Lode Runner-like screen consisting of platforms and ladders, patrolled by small spinning creatures going back and forth across the platforms, you must pick up an item and leave the screen the way you came. Unlike many other platform games, you can't jump, but instead you can dig a hole in the ground for you or an enemy to fall through. If an enemy falls through, it climbs up a ladder to the platform it came from.

As you progress, the number of nasties is increased. Each level, rendered in four-colour mode, is randomly generated, so that each session is dissimilar to the other. You have only sixty seconds to clear a level, or one of your three lives is expended.

216894.overview: As close as you'll ever get to playing Asteroids on a Dragon... this is a one player only cartridge game from the earliest days of the machine.

217067.overview: Monster Mine is a maze game viewed from above with the whole maze on the screen and you have to move about the maze collecting gold nuggets. You start at the the bottom of the mine and you need to reach one of the exits at the top of the mine. The maze is the Eldorado Gold Mine full of the nuggets but there are monsters moving about the mine that need avoiding. Each row of the mine has a monster moving along it and if you enter one of the rows then the monster will head towards you at a faster speed. If you touch a monster it is game over and each mine has a different layout every time you play.

419770.overview:
Are you a James Hunt in the making?

100 miles of tyre screechin', clutch burnin', wheel spinnin', gas guzzlin' track lie ahead as you battle your wits against the rest of the field in the Morocco Grand Prix.

446509.overview: You have been selected for this Mission because of your specialist skills in computer operations. The Aim of your Mission is to gain entry to the hidden Command complex, once there you must locate the main computer room and delete the command program by entering the Destruct Code. Intelligence informs us that this code is hidden within the complex.

446510.overview: Disrupt enemy communications and defenses by continually bombing them. The player launches from a carrier and game play is from the top-down perspective. The plane can move left, right, climb, and descend. As the player climbs to higher altitude they are safer from enemy fire. At lower altitude the plane is more susceptible to enemy fire, but bombs dropped explode closer to the front of the plane. The player must avoid SAM missiles and automatic fire from planes. The player gains points for destroying enemy cargo ships, tanks, trains, aircraft, and trucks. The player has limited bombs, and can replenish at carrier ships.

446511.overview:
MacDougal's Last Stand is an arcade game for the Dragon 32/64.

Jamie MacDougal roams the Scottish Highlands in search of his clan's lost bagpipes. Also on the moors are two sasernacks disguised as computer nasties whose aim is to stop young Jamie.

Jamie must navigate the hedges, trying to find the 16 bagpipes hidden over 16 screens. The small red nasty will always head towards the player and shoot at them. They can be destroyed by the player's attack. The player can only attack horizontally, which uses up their limited attack power. Attack power can be replenished by gathering a bagpipe. The larger nasty moves in a set pattern and can not be destroyed. The player moves to the next levels by moving through the gaps in the hedgerows.

446512.overview:
Mandragore is a 1-player side-scrolling arcade game for the Dragon 32/64.

The player controls Mandragore, a highly advanced exploration robot. During a routine investigation of an ancient pyramid, the robot inadvertently triggers the pyramid's self defense system.

446513.overview:
Essentially a clone of Moon Patrol, Moon Hopper is a speedy scrolling game where you control an armed moon buggy, rolling across a moon surface guarded by lots of aliens.

Unlike Moon Patrol, you can't control the angle of the cannon mounted on the roof, instead simply firing upwards at all times, with another gun pointing forward. Apart from the aliens, you also have craters to worry about, which must be jumped across, and junk getting in your way, which can be shot with your other cannon.

The scrolling is variable, which means that you can speed up your vehicle to avoid enemy fire. A meter at the bottom shows how far along a level you have come.

446514.overview: You stand outside a mansion which some say is haunted while others say it is cursed, and your quest is to enter and explore the mansion looking for a fabled diamond. The screen has text which describes each location you're in and you type in commands with the keyboard to interact with your surroundings.

446516.overview: The players and/or their computer opponent take turns moving on a computerized interpretation of the Monopoly board. All names have been replaced with locations in London. Players can buy and sell property, and get charged rent when they land on properties. Closely follows the rules of the original game, including: go to jail, community chest, chance, and other locations.

446518.overview:
Famed film entrepreneur Peeko Sputberg has started his quest to make movies on London's Film Row, Wardour Street. Each film's company will either help Sputberg make the film or throw him out.

At the start of the game, the player has 10 moves to find a film company that will finance the player's film. After finding a backer, the player enters an adventure game component where they must move through the production offices to find the room containing the finished script. Commands are via text entry. Each move costs 1 day and $500,000. The film must be found and completed on time and within schedule.
